subject: Signal stabilization & alert routing — CloudHarbor onboarding
messages:
From: Ariel Chen <ariel.chen@cloudharbor.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-eng@cloudharbor.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood onboarding — signal stabilization and alert routing

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudHarbor is excited to move forward. Our infra team is ready to begin the Redwood observability integration next week. We want to make sure dashboards, tracing hooks, and alert routing are set up so our on-call can rely on them from day one.

High-level asks:
- What runbook template do you expect us to fill out before handoff?
- How do we wire up traces (service / span naming) to match your dashboards?
- Can you confirm who at Redwood will own the initial alert routing and SLO tags?

Proposed kickoff: Tue 2027-06-01 10:00 PT — prefer 60m.

Attaching our current alert inventory (ops-alerts.csv).

Cheers,
Ariel Chen
Head of Platform, CloudHarbor
Ariel.chen@cloudharbor.com

Attachment: ops-alerts.csv (text/csv)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Chen <ariel.chen@cloudharbor.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding — signal stabilization and alert routing

Hi Ariel — great to hear, and thanks for the inventory.

Quick answers up front:
- Runbook: I attached our lightweight runbook template (redwood-runbook-template.md). If you can fill the incident owner list, key dashboards, and the primary escalation path, we can onboard that as the canonical runbook.
- Tracing: We recommend the service.span convention (service: <svc>, span: <handler>) and adding resource attributes: environment, deployment_id, and team. I included a short mapping doc in the Drive link below.
- Owners: Redwood will temporarily own alert routing and paging during the first two-week stabilization window. Laura Bennett (cc) will be the on-call lead for routing tweaks; Ben Carter will own runbook acceptance and SLO tagging. After stabilization we will transfer primary ownership to CloudHarbor per the MPA.

Kickoff Tue 2027-06-01 10:00 PT works — I’ll send a calendar invite. Please have the alert inventory and one sample trace (zip or link to APM) available.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-runbook-template.md (text/markdown)

---
On Sun, May 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ariel Chen <ariel.chen@cloudharbor.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudHarbor is excited to move forward. ...
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding — signal stabilization and alert routing

Adding operational details from our side so we show up prepared on Tuesday: 

Action items for internal prep:
- Ben: please pre-create the CloudHarbor dashboard folders and seed with the two templates: 1) service health overview, 2) latency & tail-latency by endpoint. I left notes in the Drive link on widget queries.
- Neha: prepare the tracing mapping snippet (service/span name) and a policy doc for which spans we will instrument for KV cache misses and long-tail ops.
- Sean: I’ll draft the escalation matrix and a short play for PagerDuty routing (two-tier: Redwood primary, CloudHarbor secondary). We should include an auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant if token generation latency exceeds SLO for >3 minutes — that reduces customer impact while we triage.

Timeline: allocate 90 minutes internal prep on Mon afternoon (3pm PT). We’ll join the kickoff with these artifacts ready.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Chen <ariel.chen@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 14:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding — signal stabilization and alert routing

Hi Ariel — good sync today, thanks for the time. Summary and next steps below so both teams have a single source of truth.

Summary of decisions:
- Stabilization window: Tue 2027-06-01 to Tue 2027-06-15 (14 days). Redwood will own alert routing and paging for that period and will hand over to CloudHarbor on 2027-06-16 pending a checklist.
- Runbook: CloudHarbor to fill the attached runbook (sections: incident owner, impact matrix, mitigation steps, rollback plan) by 2027-06-03 EOD. Ben will perform acceptance review and mark the runbook as green or provide edits within 24 hours.
- Dashboards: Redwood created a working folder at the Drive link. Ben created the service-health and latency dashboards and shared edit access.
- Tracing: Agreed on service/span naming (service:cloudharbor.<svc>, span:handler.<operation>) and resource attributes. Neha will push a small instrumentation checklist for language-specific SDKs.
- Alerts: Initial routing will page Redwood SRE group. We will implement two routing tiers and an auto-fallback rule for model variant degradation (>3m sustained high tail latency).

Deliverables & due dates:
- CloudHarbor: completed runbook (redwood-runbook-template.md) + sample trace: 2027-06-03 EOD
- Redwood: final alert-routing-matrix.csv and dashboard wiring diagram: 2027-06-04 12:00 PT
- Joint: stabilization retrospective meeting and handover decision: 2027-06-16 09:00 PT

Attachments (sent): redwood-runbook-template.md, dashboard-wiring-diagram.pdf, alert-routing-matrix.csv

Drive folder: https://drive.redwoodinc.com/teams/onboarding/CloudHarbor/signal-stabilization
JIRA: OPS-4721

Thanks — we’ll standby for the runbook and sample traces.

— Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
